item.title: Zero Trust Doesn't Fully Solve the Agentic AI Problem
item.content:encoded: Zero Trust security was designed around identities accessing resources. Agentic AI introduces a different challenge: autonomous systems that reason, plan, and execute actions with real-world consequences. This article explores emerging risks including prompt injection, tool misuse, privilege chaining, and auditability gaps, and proposes an agentic security framework built around action authorization, behavioral baselines, reasoning transparency, and human checkpoints.

item.title: Let AI Models Fight Over Your Architecture
item.content:encoded: Asking a single AI to design your system is a mistake. Single prompts yield generic, happy-path answers. Instead, developers should build multi-agent workflows where specialized AIs—like an Architect, Red-Team, and Evaluator, actively debate the architecture. By forcing LLMs to propose, critique, and score tradeoffs against simpler baselines, you avoid brittle chatbot responses. The result is an automated architecture review board that outputs production-ready Decision Records.

item.title: Suffering From Marketing Paralysis? Everyone Is Right Now, Here’s The Way Out
item.content:encoded: Open-ended AI development cycles open competitive space as marketers contend with the lack of traditional SaaS launch sequences and evolving go to market strategy. A cohort-based process aligns with AI development and sales, with dynamic, customer-informed narratives.

item.title: Building a Read-Only AI Agent for Storage Incident Response
item.content:encoded: Agentic AI can be useful in cloud storage operations, but its first production role should be read-only investigation rather than auto-remediation. This article argues for giving AI agents access to metrics, logs, traces, deployments, tickets, and topology so they can produce structured incident briefs with timelines, blast radius, ranked hypotheses, confidence scores, and auditable evidence while leaving production changes to human engineers.

item.title: Hands-Off Coding on GCP: Building Autonomous Agents with Guardrails
item.content:encoded: This article outlines an architecture for autonomous background coding agents built on Google Cloud Platform. Rather than focusing on prompting alone, it frames AI coding as an orchestration and infrastructure problem involving isolated runtimes, deterministic workflows, secure execution environments, task queues, observability, and pull-request automation. Using services like Cloud Run Jobs, Vertex AI, Cloud Workflows, Firestore, and Secret Manager, the piece argues that reliable AI software development depends more on process discipline and governance than raw model capability.

item.title: How I Built a Pipeline to Restore Old B&W Photos to 4K Color Using Open-Source AI
item.content:encoded: I tested 8 different open-source AI upscalers and restoration tools to find the best pipeline for converting old black-and-white film footage into 4K colorized images for a YouTube history channel. After days of testing on rented GPU servers, the winning pipeline is surprisingly simple: Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 does everything — upscale, restore, AND colorize — in a single prompt, in under 60 seconds.

item.title: Every Tool You Give an AI Agent Becomes a Security Decision
item.content:encoded: As AI agents gain access to tools and real-world systems, traditional chatbot security models become insufficient. This article argues that sensitive actions should never rely solely on model output. Instead, authorization, validation, policy enforcement, audit logging, and business-rule checks should sit outside the model and as close as possible to the tool being invoked. The goal is simple: the agent requests, deterministic controls decide, and the tool executes only if allowed.

item.title: The Math Behind RevShare vs Flat-Fee Partner Compensation (And Why Most Teams Model It Wrong)

CPA is predictable but decouples partner incentives from customer quality. RevShare aligns incentives but compounds costs over time and introduces negative balance carryover — a policy decision with massive financial impact. The crossover point (the customer lifetime at which RevShare total commission equals the CPA) is the single most important number in your model. This article provides the Python models, crossover calculation, and the framework for building real-time comparison into your system.

This article covers the protocol-level mechanics, production code patterns for each failure mode, and why monitoring is the actual product — not the tracking setup itself.

item.title: Most Node.js Apps Using ClamAV Have the Same Bug. Here's What It Is.
item.content:encoded:
Calling ClamAV from Node.js looks easy: spawn clamscan, check the exit code, done. But the standard implementation has a silent bug — exit code 2 means "scan could not complete," not "clean," and almost every custom wrapper collapses it into one of the other two outcomes. The result is a false-clean verdict on encrypted archives, permission-denied files, and timeouts. The fix is to model ClamAV's three real outcomes — Clean, Malicious, ScanError — as three explicit return values, and force the caller to handle ScanError as a security decision rather than a programming error. This article explains why this matters, what the failure looks like in production, and what a correct minimal wrapper looks like in practice.
